name: Thetanuts Finance
rootCause: Index vault component-share accounting flaw. Lost: 105471.50 USDC

descriptions.text: Index vault component-share accounting flaw. Lost: 105471.50 USDC

The Thetanuts index vault lets holders claim() a proportional basket of underlying component-vault shares (BTC/ETH/AVAX/BNB/MATIC USD vaults) for their index shares, and mint() new index shares by depositing component shares. The accounting is broken: an attacker can claim out the component shares and then re-mint replacement index shares while the component-vault transfer amounts pulled by mint stay at zero (the mint does not actually charge/transfer the component shares it should). The attacker flash-loans nearly the entire index-share balance from Aave's aToken, claims the component shares from the borrowed index shares, then loops mint() to fabricate enough index shares to repay the Aave flash loan - at no real cost. After repaying the loan, the claimed component vault shares (later converted to USDC via initWithdraw) plus residual shares are pure profit, ~105,471 USDC. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0xbba9f138fe39503bfd1aa62932dbd6ab35d37d23d48e4b7bf2988a9d5dc39fec Analysis: https://x.com/PeckShieldAlert/status/2066540451126190312

A legacy vault of Thetanuts Finance on Ethereum was exploited due to a flaw in redemption math and integer calculations in the mint/claim functions. The attacker used flash loans to drain approximately $2.1 million after reducing token supply to near zero. A whitehat recovered most funds (~$2M), resulting in a net loss of around $105K according to the project. Current products and active contracts were unaffected.

Thetanuts Finance's deprecated options vault on Ethereum was exploited for $2.1M through a rounding bug in share/claim accounting, allowing free minting and redemption of option tokens. Most funds were recovered by a white-hat. The legacy vault's mint logic performed integer division that could round deposit amounts to zero under specific low-supply states, enabling attackers to repeatedly mint new option tokens without paying for collateral.
